User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the Contador de Quesitos app.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

username.description: The user's chosen username. Must be unique.

avatar.description: URL or path to the user's chosen avatar image.

Quesito.title: Quesito
Quesito.description: Represents a single 'quesito' added to the global list.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Quesito entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who added this quesito. (Relationship: User 1:N Quesito)

instagramUsername.description: The Instagram username associated with this quesito.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the quesito was added.

definition.description: Stores user profiles. The userId is used to identify the user.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user.

definition.description: Stores all quesitos added by users. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: quesitoId
params.description: The unique identifier of the quesito.

firestore.reasoning:
This design prioritizes security and scalability for the 'Contador de Quesitos' app. It leverages path-based ownership and structural segregation to simplify security rules and ensure data integrity.  

`/users/{userId}`:  Each user has their own document. This collection stores user profiles and enables user-specific data.  The `userId` in the path serves as the unique identifier and links the user to their 'quesitos'.

`/quesitos/{quesitoId}`: Stores all quesitos added by users.  The `userId` is denormalized into each quesito document to ensure authorization independence.  This enables efficient listing of all quesitos. The `userId` field enables filtering quesitos by user if needed.

This structure achieves Authorization Independence by including the `userId` in the `quesitos` collection, avoiding the need for `get()` calls in security rules to verify ownership. It supports QAPs by allowing secure listing of quesitos and ensures only authenticated users can create them. By using a flat `quesitos` collection and denormalizing the `userId`, listing all quesitos is efficient and doesn't require complex queries. The structure also allows filtering quesitos by `userId` if that functionality is needed.
